The five obsolete-machine/code-talker map labels were never reintroduced by a later commit. [7d79fd1 (26 April)](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/cipher-museum/commit/7d79fd11a6f52a8f0da93fe5171d659266559e60) introduced the map badges. [60337b5 (4 August)](https://github.com/systemslibrarian/cipher-museum/commit/60337b5ca7e16160908b96bdb337aa564f68e9d4) corrected their exhibit headers but missed the duplicated map rows. The independent review at `9441865` also found incomplete centralization and an inconsistent service-worker stamp; the final repair reverified and corrected those findings.

`data/exhibit-trust.json` now owns each exhibit’s classification, and `data/trust-labels.json` owns all four names, icons, and definitions. The shared loader and generators produce exhibit headers and facts, every hall card, map rows and legend, search metadata, comparison classifications and filters, and artifact metadata. Shared browser rendering uses the generated trust objects for search, comparison, and artifact cards. Legacy security badges are removed; context entries render no trust badge, including Aeneas’s hall card and the separate Freemason cultural exhibit. Related links and the sitemap introduce no independent trust classifications. Descriptive history, attack evidence, and limitations remain separate from classifications.

- Scytale, Caesar, Polybius, Pigpen, Bacon, Tap Code, Atbash, and ROT13 retain **Broken**. Caesar no longer displays contradictory badges.
- SIGABA, Typex, KL-7, Fialka, and Navajo use **Historical Only**. “Never publicly broken” belongs in qualified exhibit prose.
- Historical Only has the exact shared definition **“No longer in use, or never confirmed broken/deciphered.”** All displayed definitions and tooltips are generated from it.
- Search uses a neutral **Trust:** prefix and omits context classifications. Search and artifact builders read canonical data directly, so legacy status cannot override it.
- Comparison no longer gives Navajo or SIGABA independent classifications. Chaocipher’s artifact history reflects the published 2016 attacks. Great Cipher prose names Bazeries, 1893, syllabic analysis and cribs; Chaocipher names Lasry, Rubin, Kopal and Wacker, 2016, and the documented attack types.

The reviewed `cipher-museum-f028d3aa` stamp came from CRLF copies of `favicon.svg`, `js/breadcrumbs.js`, and `js/ui-delegates.js`; committed LF assets produced `6c3297cb`. The hash generator now canonicalizes CRLF to LF only for the text asset types it hashes, preserving binary bytes. There is no hardcoded expected hash or repository-wide renormalization. The final generated PR #1 version is **`cipher-museum-9664d4d3`**. Trust/search/artifact runtime assets are included in the cache/hash inventory. A fresh checkout reproduces this version.

The timing-coverage failure was reproduced on Node 22: **26 engines measurable against the old minimum of 40; zero scaling violations**. The old 20 ms baseline and 200 KB cap excluded fast engines, making coverage depend on the environment. Calibrated repeated CPU-time batches now compare 25 KB with 100 KB using identical repeat counts. The **10× scaling limit remains unchanged**, and coverage now requires **all 85 registry engines**, with no silent skips. A real quadratic canary exceeds the limit and is rejected; missing/invalid-key coverage and weakening the guard to 40 are also rejected. Both test runners continue through later suites after failures.

Validation at `663cbffe736b88353ac4d17ecff300c5d6ae665e`, using supported **Node 22.23.3**:

- Required trust/search/artifact/count/minification generators ran; outputs are idempotent and freshness checks pass.
- `npm test`: every suite passed, including all suites after the timing guard; **85 measured, zero skipped, zero scaling violations**.
- Corpus replay: **100,026 records; 99,500 pass, 526 documented known deviations, zero unexplained deviations**.
- `npm run lint:html`: **197 files, zero errors**; `git diff --check`: clean.
- **13 isolated deliberate mutations rejected**: Caesar policy, forbidden modern entry, duplicate legacy badge, Aeneas context badge, legacy search metadata, Broken search prefix, Navajo comparison classification, stale Chaocipher artifact history, copied artifact/legend definitions, changed Historical Only wording, CRLF-dependent hashing, and weakened timing coverage. The real quadratic canary is additional.
- Fresh committed LF checkout: service-worker version, complete rendered trust audit, and generated metadata freshness all pass.

The secure allowlist is exactly these nine identities; no additions:

| # | Entry | Correct-use justification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 36 | One-Time Pad | Perfect secrecy requires a uniformly random, secret, message-length pad used exactly once. |
| 37 | Vernam | Secure only under those OTP conditions; XOR alone, repeating tape, or pad reuse is insufficient. |
| 60 | Diffie–Hellman | Vetted groups, strong secret exponents, and authentication are required for secure key agreement. |
| 61 | RSA | Adequate key sizes, secure padding, and correct key handling are required. |
| 62 | AES | Secure modes, nonce discipline, and protected keys are required. |
| 63 | SHA-256 | Resists practical collision and preimage attacks; it is a hash, with secure use depending on the application. |
| 158 | ECDSA | Vetted curves, protected keys, and correctly generated, never-reused nonces are required. |
| 159 | Shamir’s Secret Sharing | Fewer than the threshold shares reveal no secret when coefficients are uniformly random in the correct field. |
| 160 | Zero-Knowledge Proofs | The selected protocol’s assumptions, setup, parameters, and implementation must hold. |

All changed roster/header classifications are below, plus Voynich/Dorabella metadata corrections. Old labels show **map / header** when they differ. **None** means the badge is omitted.
